pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic Ultrasound revealing a 4 cm mature ovarian teratoma (dermoid cyst) containing ectopic neural tissue, along with positive CSF anti-GluN1 antibodies. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient had an underlying, asymptomatic ovarian teratoma containing ectopic nervous tissue. The immune system recognized this neural tissue as foreign, generating IgG antibodies against the GluN1 subunit of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors. These autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to NMDA receptors in the brain, causing receptor cross-linking and internalisation. This selectively reduces NMDA receptor density on post-synaptic membranes, preferentially disrupting GABAergic inhibitory pathways. The loss of frontostriatal inhibition triggers dopamine dysregulation (psychosis and dyskinesias) and central autonomic disinhibition, culminating in catastrophic neuro-psychiatric collapse. Treatment requires prompt surgical removal of the teratoma combined with high-dose immunotherapy.
